lines: Armor jokes need padding. Otherwise everyone feels the <jump>point</jump> too soon.
Armor jokes need timing. Mine usually arrive with iron on them.
I keep a spare joke near the forge. It is not always ready for public use.
I told a joke at the forge once. The workstation took it better than the villagers did.
People say I work too much. I say the work is the only one here that listens.
If confidence could be traded, this village would be rich and still somehow underprepared.
I tried taking a day off. The village immediately treated it like an emergency drill.
A good joke needs timing. Around here, timing usually trips over a chicken.
I would laugh louder, but someone would ask me to explain it and ruin everything.
The bell has one joke. It screams, and everyone suddenly remembers they have legs.
Armor jokes are hard to land. Too much plating.
I tried a lighter joke once, but it lacked protection.
My best helmet joke went over everyone's head, as intended.
A shield walked into the square and took the hit for the punchline.
I would tell a forge joke, but it is still cooling.
Most armor humor is layered. That is why nobody laughs quickly.
I made a joke from scrap metal. It still had sharp edges.
The anvil laughed once. Terrible sound. Very sincere.
A buckle joke only works if it holds together.
I know a chainmail joke, but it has too many links.
The forge and I have an understanding. I sweat and it complains.
I asked the helmet for advice. It said to keep my head in it.
A polished breastplate is just a mirror that chose violence.
If sparks were applause, I would be famous and slightly on fire.
I made greaves for a joke once. It still ran away.
